cues: Everything haloalkanes do starts with one polar bond.
Halogen is more electronegative than carbon, so the carbon is slightly positive and the halogen slightly negative.
A nucleophile, an electron rich species like hydroxide, cyanide or ammonia, attacks that positive carbon, and the halide leaves with the bonding pair.
text: Everything haloalkanes do starts with one polar bond. Halogen is more electronegative than carbon, so the carbon is slightly positive and the halogen slightly negative. A nucleophile, an electron rich species like hydroxide, cyanide or ammonia, attacks that positive carbon, and the halide leaves with the bonding pair. This is nucleophilic substitution.
